{{nihongo|'''Ninomiya Shrine'''|二宮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

In ancient times, it was also called ``Miyama Myojin'' or ``Ninomiya Myojin''. </ref>.

== Enshrined God ==
The enshrined deity is listed according to the shrine history book. 
* '''{{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Kenhaya Susano no Mikoto}}'''
* '''{{ill|Kushinadahime|Q505469|qid=Q505469|lt=Kushiinada Hime no Mikoto}}'''
* '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi no Mikoto}}'''
* '''{{ill|Fujiwara no Tokihira|Q2994735|qid=Q2994735|lt=Fujiwara Tokihira Mikoto}}'''
:According to legend, when {{ill|Fujiwara no Moritsune|Q11623227|qid=Q11623227}}, who was demoted in 4th year ({{ill|1180|Q19702|qid=Q19702}}), settled in this area, he enshrined his ancestor, Fujiwara Tokihira, in his side hall. Since Tokihira is a political enemy of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}} (Tenjin), it is said that the parishioners of Tenjin did not visit the shrine <ref name="place name"/>.
* '''{{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119|lt=Daisaku no Mikoto}}'''
:{{ill|Meiji era|lt=Meiji period|qid=Q3125096}} Wakamiya Hachiman Shrine, a nearby mukakusha, was {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|ja|合祀|qid=Q11412524}}.
* '''{{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondabetsu no Mikoto}}'''
:In the Meiji period, Setsusha and Awa Hachiman Shrine were enshrined together.

== History ==
According to the shrine's legend, the <ref name="historical history book"> shrine history book was founded by the imperial order of {{ill|Emperor Saga|Q316654|qid=Q316654}} during the {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}} years ({{ill|810|Q23819|qid=Q23819}} to {{ill|824|Q30353|qid=Q30353}}). </ref>. Like place names, the name ``Miyama'' appeared to be ``Miyama'' in ancient times, and was attributed to our company. {{ill|Miyama clan|Q11355183|qid=Q11355183}} served as {{ill|Shinkan (official)|Q11589454|qid=Q11589454}} for generations. <ref> ``Chiba Prefecture place name'' Miyama Village. </ref>.``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' from the middle of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmeicho}} states: Samukawa Shrine", but our company is said to be {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}}. It is also said that it was revered by the imperial court as {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ninomiya}} of {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆسا|cs|Provincie Šimósa|de|Provinz Shimousa|es|Provincia de Shimōsa|fa|ولایت شیموسا|fr|Province de Shimōsa|gl|Provincia de Shimōsa|hak|Shimōsa-koet|id|Provinsi Shimousa|it|Shimōsa|ja|下総国|ko|시모사국|lt|Šimosos žemė|nl|Shimosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimōsa|ru|Симоса (провинция)|simple|Shimōsa Province|sk|Šimósa|sr|Провинција Шимоса|tr|Shimōsa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоса|zh|下總國|zh_min_nan|Simôsa-kok|zh_yue|下總國|qid=Q1053695}} (however, {{ill|Tamasaki Shrine|Q11572538|qid=Q11572538}} of {{ill|Asahi, Chiba|Q637868|qid=Q637868}} is also called Ninomiya). It is unknown when it began to be called Ninomiya Shrine, but (Japan)|Q1327472|Inuigen}} 2 ({{ill|1303|Q5614|qid=Q5614}}) The temple bell (stored in Shohoin, Narita City) says ``Soshu Ninomiya == Approach ==
[[File:Ninomiya-Shrine.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Sando]]
When you approach the shrine from the torii gate in front of the shrine, the approach becomes lower and then crosses the valley. Furthermore, a stream flows at the bottom of the valley, and the water vein is said to lead to a pond within the grounds of {{ill|Kikuta Shrine|Q11619900|qid=Q11619900}}, which is enshrined in {{ill|Tsudanuma|Q7849928|qid=Q7849928}} in {{ill|Narashino|Q318047|qid=Q318047}}. If you walk along the valley floor in a straight line, by the time you reach the top of the stone steps, you will be able to see the Karahafu facing the worship hall, and the master carpenter's {{ill|Design|Q82604|qid=Q82604}} has been ingenious so that you can take your time to admire the large, majestic {{ill|Karahafu|Q977293|qid=Q977293}} curves and the majestic carvings.

== Festival ==
* {{ill|Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824}} (January 1st)
* Oshahatsu Festival (January 7th)
* Otsutsu porridge cooking ritual (January 14th)
* {{ill|Setsubun|Q746798|qid=Q746798|lt=Setsubun Festival}} (February 3rd)
* '''Regular Festival''' (October 16th)
* '''Daikaage'' (Obiyo, {{ill|Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|Q11511066|qid=Q11511066}}night of November 13th)
:A festival named after the bonfires lit by villagers to welcome Fujiwara no Moritsune and others who were said to have been exiled to this area.
* '''{{ill|Shimōsa Miyama Seven-Year Festival|Q11361280|qid=Q11361280}}''' (Year of the Ox/Year of the Wild)

== Cultural assets ==

== Chiba Prefecture designated intangible folk cultural property ==
* {{ill|Shimōsa Miyama Seven-Year Festival|Q11361280|qid=Q11361280}} - Designated on March 30, 2004.

== Cultural property designated by Funabashi City ==
* Shrine building (tangible cultural property (building)) - Designated on February 27, 1992.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Saito Sonojo}} etc. dedicated haiku plaque (tangible cultural property (historical material)) - Designated on October 23, 1980.
* Ninomiya Shrine Kagura (Intangible Folk Cultural Property) - Designated on June 26, 1995.
* Ginkgo at Ninomiya Shrine (natural monument) - Designated on March 30, 2012.

== Transportation access ==
* {{ill|Tsudanuma Station|Q801534|qid=Q801534}} ({{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}}{{ill|Sōbu Main Line|Q1191364|qid=Q1191364}}) From the north exit
** Take the {{ill|Keisei Bus|Q11374367|qid=Q11374367}} (Tsu 02 bound for Ninomiya Shrine) and get off at the final stop, "Ninomiya Shrine" (ride time: 20 minutes)
** Take the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Funabashi Shinkeisei Bus}} (Tsu 08 bound for Ninomiya Jinja-mae) and get off at the final stop, "Ninomiya-jinja-mae" (20 minute ride)
* From {{ill|Yakuendai Station|Q8047226|qid=Q8047226}} ({{ill|Keisei Matsudo Line|Q3553734|qid=Q3553734}})
** Walk (3 minutes) from the Yakuendai Station Iriguchi bus stop on National Route 296, take the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Funabashi Shinkeisei Bus}} (Tsu 08 bound for Ninomiya Jinja-mae) and get off at the final stop, Ninomiya-jinja-mae (10 minute ride)
* From {{ill|Keisei Ōkubo Station|Q6383851|qid=Q6383851}} ({{ill|Keisei Main Line|Q1063675|qid=Q1063675}})
** Walk (7 minutes) from the Toho Daigaku-mae bus stop, take {{ill|Keisei Bus|Q11374367|qid=Q11374367}} (Tsu 02 bound for Ninomiya Shrine) and get off at the final stop, Ninomiya Shrine (ride time: 6 minutes)
*: Keisei buses near Keisei Okubo Station have different routes for going down and going up. The nearest bus stop for going down is "Toho Daigaku-mae" and the nearest bus stop for going up is "Okubo Jujiro".
